summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later open reversal) and chronic abdominal pain/nausea presented with acute worsening midepigastric pain, nausea, and non-bloody vomiting after stopping her GERD medications, with brief diarrhea prior to arrival. CT abdomen/pelvis showed no obstruction or post-surgical complication; surgery found no indication for intervention. Gastroenterology felt symptoms were most consistent with bile reflux gastritis related to post-surgical anatomy and recommended bowel rest, IV PPI transitioned to oral PPI twice daily, sucralfate, ranitidine, and small frequent meals; inpatient EGD was deferred in favor of planned outpatient endoscopy. Hospital course was notable for low-normal blood sugars with shakiness that improved with dextrose-containing IV fluids and resumption of oral intake, transient hypotension that improved with IV fluids and stopping IV morphine, and temporary IV levetiracetam while unable to swallow pills. She improved to tolerating small meals without significant nausea/vomiting and was discharged home on intensified acid suppression and non-opioid-focused pain control with GI follow-up.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
